#### The sixth egress grant — C10, recorded before the request made under it *(v1.8.19)*

**It lands after Phase 3's close, and that is stated rather than smoothed over.** C10 was opened by an outside review (v1.8.16, item 33(d)) *after* the phase had already produced its results, and this document is not going to reopen a closed phase to make the paperwork tidy. The grant sits here, adjacent to the phase whose finding it scopes, labelled as post-close.

**The ordering discipline is unchanged and is the whole point.** This entry is committed and pushed **before** the first request made under it, as the first five grants were (v1.8.1, v1.8.3, v1.8.5, v1.8.8, v1.8.11). §Corrections item 34's fourth-grant note states the rule plainly: *"a grant written afterwards is a description, not an authorization."*

**What it buys, and the question it settles.** One arm: **`claude-haiku-4-5`'s time to response headers**, over the six synthetic `LiveMain` fixtures at the standard 8 repeats — 48 orders, the same shape as every prior hosted run, which keeps it poolable with them. C2 closed on the finding that the **fixed term alone** — time to headers, before one token exists — is mean **3,157 ms** / p95 **6,917 ms**, exceeding the ≤ 2.5 s target on its own. **Both arms behind that number are `claude-sonnet-5`, and §Success metrics' ≤ 2.5 s row is Haiku's.** What this measures is whether the *cause* C2 closes on is Haiku's cause or only Sonnet's.

**Both outcomes are written down in advance, because only one of them is comfortable.**

| If Haiku's headers time is… | Then |
|---|---|
| **≳ 2.5 s** | C2's conclusion generalises. The target is unreachable by any prompt-side change on the default model too, and item 33(d)'s rescoping was cautious rather than necessary |
| **≪ 2.5 s** | **C2's stated cause does NOT hold for the default model.** The latency row still reads MISSED — 4,615 ms p95 is measured, on Haiku, and is not in dispute — but *"unreachable by any prompt-side change"* would be a Sonnet property that this document had generalised, and the miss would return to being unexplained on the model that ships |

**The second row is the one worth paying for.** A grant that can only confirm what the document already believes is not worth $0.07; this one can take a closed row's explanation away from it.

**What it costs, derived rather than quoted.** At the post-C3 per-order figures in §Cost model — 5,118 cached tokens at 0.1×, ~179.7 uncached input at 1×, ~106.2 output at 5×, on Haiku's $1 / $5 per MTok — one order is **≈$0.001223**. Forty-eight orders is **≈$0.059**, plus a single cache write at 1.25× (**≈$0.0064**), for **≈$0.065**. **Cap: $0.10.** Against **≈$2.50** remaining. *(The C10 row's standing "≈$0.10" estimate is retained as the cap and is not the derivation.)*

**The boundary, unchanged from the third, fourth, and fifth grants.** It covers the **six synthetic situation fixtures** in `tests/live/LiveMain.cpp` — invented values in the same field set as a real snapshot — and **not** real scenario state from a deployed mission file. `run-live-scenario.ps1` is not run under this grant. C1 released that boundary once, by an explicit owner decision, for a run this document had held across four grants; **a later grant does not inherit it**, and treating "the fields match" as authorization is the inference §Tenet 4's gate exists to prevent.

**What this grant does not authorize.** No doctrine comparison — the two-arm doctrine question is **null on all three estimators** (item 29) and re-running it is the third pair of arms the fifth grant already refused. No `claude.maxTokens` change, no latency-target change, no config default change. **Measurement only**, as all five before it. And no second arm follows from a disappointing first: if the number lands in the band where it settles nothing, that is the result.

**One thing this grant fixes that the previous five did not.** The bodies it replays are **regenerated at Haiku**, not the archived Sonnet ones. `tests/live/measure-ttft.ps1` has no model parameter — the model is *inside* the dumped body — so replaying the archived arms would have measured `claude-sonnet-5` a third time while reporting it as Haiku. That is item 33(d)'s error in a new costume, and it is named here so the run cannot commit it by accident. `--mode ttft-dump` **sends nothing and needs no key**, so regenerating the bodies is free and offline.

#### The standing hosted-egress authorization — **DRAFT, NOT IN FORCE** *(v1.8.44, drafted 2026-08-09)*

> # ⚠ NOTHING MAY BE RUN UNDER THIS SECTION.
>
> **This is a draft put in front of the owner for a decision. It is not a grant, it authorizes
> nothing, and no hosted request may be made under it.** The §Review checklist box it addresses
> **stays unticked** until an owner records a decision here, and this banner is what a later reader
> needs in order not to mistake a proposal for an authorization. **A grant written afterwards is a
> description, not an authorization** (§Corrections item 34) — and a grant nobody signed is not even
> a description.

**What the outstanding box is actually asking, which is not what the six grants answered.** All six
egress grants — v1.8.1, v1.8.3, v1.8.5, v1.8.8, v1.8.11 and v1.8.19 — **authorize measurement**, each
says so in its own text, and each is scoped to named experiments with a derived cost and a cap.
v1.8.19 states that **a later grant does not inherit an earlier one's boundary.** So there is no
authorization under which this plugin may run the hosted backend **as a product** — for someone
operating a scenario rather than measuring one — and that is a different kind of permission rather
than a larger amount of the same one. **The right posture for a project still measuring itself is
exactly the one it has**, and this box has been correctly unticked for its whole life.

##### The finding that changes what this grant has to contain

**There is no spend ceiling anywhere in the shipped code.** `CommanderConfig.h` carries
`claude.enabled`, `claude.model`, `claude.maxTokens` and `claude.apiKeyEnvVar`; there is no
per-run, per-day or cumulative cost bound, and no counter that could enforce one. **The `$5` budget
this document tracks is a convention maintained by hand in §Cost model, enforced by nothing.**

Under six measurement grants that was safe, and it was safe for a reason worth naming: **each run was
individually authorized, individually costed and individually recorded, so a human checkpoint sat in
front of every request this project ever made.** **A standing authorization removes exactly that
checkpoint** — which is the point of it — so it has to put something in its place.

**What the existing controls do and do not bound, derived rather than asserted.** `commander.cadenceS`
(20 s) and `claude.maxTokens` (512) bound the request *rate* and the per-request *size*, so the cost
of a run is bounded by its length: at the post-C3 per-order figure of **≈$0.001223** and two commanded
entities, one order each per cadence is **6 orders/min ≈ $0.0073/min ≈ $0.44/hour**. A ten-minute
smoke is **≈$0.073**. **What nothing bounds is the number of runs.** Against the **≈$2.43** remaining
of the $5 budget, that is about **5.5 hours** of continuous two-entity commanding — **so a scenario
left running overnight with the commander enabled exceeds this project's entire budget by roughly
2×, and no code path would notice.**

##### The three decisions this grant contains, separated so they can be answered separately

They are genuinely independent, and bundling them is how a governance decision gets made by accident.

| # | The decision | What "yes" costs | What "no" costs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. The data boundary** | May **real scenario state from an arbitrary deployed mission** leave this machine, standingly? C1 released this boundary **once**, by explicit owner decision (v1.8.11), for **one named run** | Every hosted run thereafter transmits position, velocity, course, team, reported tracks and loadout drawn from a live mission — which inherits the release tree's proprietary classification | The hosted path stays a measurement instrument and never ships to anyone |
| **2. Standing vs per-run** | Does one authorization cover an indefinite series, or does each run keep its own record? | The per-run human checkpoint disappears, and with it the only spend control that exists | Every hosted run needs a PRD revision first — which is the discipline that has held for six grants and has never once been the bottleneck |
| **3. Who holds it** | The owner personally, or **anyone in possession of the release tree**? | `claude.enabled=true` in a deployed config is then a sufficient authorization by itself | The grant names people, and a deployment by anyone else is unauthorized regardless of config |

##### What a grant would have to carry to be safe, if the answer to all three is yes

**These are conditions rather than suggestions, and each names the failure it prevents.**

1. **A cumulative spend ceiling enforced in code, not in this document.** A standing grant whose only
   limit is a number in §Cost model is a standing grant with no limit. **This does not exist today
   and would have to be built** — a counter, a configured ceiling, and a refusal that turns
   `claude.enabled` off rather than merely logging. *(Prevents: the overnight scenario above.)*
2. **The transmitted-field list is re-reviewed against the mission actually deployed, not against
   `docs/egress.md`'s example.** The enumerated list is a property of the snapshot builder; **which
   scenario's values fill it is a property of whoever deploys.** *(Prevents: a grant reviewed against
   "Mariana Shield" being read as covering a classified laydown.)*
3. **The repository-visibility answer travels with it.** §Review checklist records the repository as
   private, **checked 2026-08-07**, and notes that publication needs the same authorization as the
   hosted backend. **These two boxes are the same decision seen from two sides** — what may leave the
   machine — and answering one without the other leaves the weaker of the two governing.

##### What this draft explicitly does **not** propose

**It does not propose a default change.** `commander.enabled` and `claude.enabled` both stay `false`
in the shipped default config and in `data/config/plugins/`, under every answer above. **A standing
authorization is permission to turn something on; it is not turning it on**, and the Operational
readiness checklist's two config boxes are unaffected.

**It does not propose that this grant be used by this session or any automated one.** Nothing here
changes the standing instruction that `-Backend claude` needs a recorded owner grant **before** the
request.

##### How this box gets ticked

**By an owner writing a decision into this document and committing it before any request made under
it** — the same ordering discipline as the six grants, which every one of them met. **A decision to
say no is as complete an answer as a decision to say yes**, and would tick the box just as well: the
box asks for a decision, not for a permission. What it cannot be is left implicit, because
**`claude.enabled` is one line in a config file and the only thing currently standing between it and
a live request is that nobody has written it.**

### Maintenance — the phased work is finished *(v1.8.41, owner decision 2026-08-09)*

> **THIS IS THE CLOSE OF THE PHASED PERIOD, AND IT IS WRITTEN AT THE CLOSE RATHER THAN AT AN OPEN,
> which is the one thing Phase 3 got wrong and this section is deliberately not repeating.** Phase 3
> closed at v1.8.17. Twenty-four revisions followed with no phase, no gate and no close condition —
> productive ones, which closed C5, C8, C11–C16, C18–C22 and C23's engineering — but **with no state
> the project could be in other than "here is what is still open".** A defect register is never empty
> by construction, so "are we done?" had no answerable form. **It has one now.**

**The decision: no further phase is planned. The product is feature-complete against this document's
FR set, and what remains is response to what breaks.**

**What that claim rests on, so it can be checked rather than believed.** Every FR carries acceptance
criteria and a `UAC-` entry. All nine open questions are resolved or dispositioned. Every §Success
metrics row has a verdict, an instrument and a date. The register is down to two rows and neither is
engineering. `tools/lint-prd.ps1` (11 checks) and `tools/check-artifacts.ps1` pass with zero
warnings, the unit suite is green, and since v1.8.40 CI compiles the measurement harness too.

**What changes, concretely:**

1. **The register is the only tracker**, under the entry rule in §Carried out of Phase 3: a row needs
   a named mechanism or a named decider. Nothing else opens one.
2. **§Success metrics freezes.** Each row keeps its verdict, its instrument and its measurement date.
   **A metric is re-measured when its instrument or its subject changes — not on a calendar**, and
   never by quotation. `tools/acceptance-report.py` owns the in-engine figure and the linter owns its
   agreement across three documents.
3. **`tools/lint-prd.ps1` and CI are the standing guard.** They already catch version drift, sentinel
   disagreement, requirement smells, FR↔UAC parity and — since v1.8.40 — instrument rot.
4. **No new deliverable list, and no gate.** There is nothing to pass, which is the point.

**What this deliberately gives up, stated because it is the cost and not a footnote.** **It forecloses
the outcome question.** What the commander is *worth* stands permanently at **unmeasured** — the first
unconfounded comparison returned a null at n = 1 (item 47(b)), the repeat refuted the identity without
replacing it (item 50(a)), and the two post-fix runs are n = 2 with intervals that overlap almost
entirely. **Anyone later asking "is this worth deploying?" gets no answer from this document, and that
is now a permanent property of it rather than a gap someone is closing.** The runs cost ~35 minutes
and nothing else; **reopening the question needs only an owner who wants it, and this paragraph is
where they should start.**

> ***(v1.8.42 — THE OWNER WANTED IT, AND THIS PARAGRAPH IS WHERE THEY STARTED. §Corrections item
> 58.)*** **The outcome question is reopened by owner decision on 2026-08-09.** The protocol is
> §Validation's *"The outcome campaign — a pre-registration"*, written in full **before** its first
> run: primary endpoint, paired design, n = 4, decision rule, minimum detectable effect, null
> wording, two forbidden claims and the provenance disclosure.
>
> **Maintenance is NOT rescinded and nothing above is withdrawn.** No phase opens. No gate is
> created. The register stays empty and its entry rule is untouched. No bar moves, and the paragraph
> above remains the correct description of what this document said until today. **What "permanent"
> turned out to mean is "until somebody decides otherwise", which is what the sentence about an
> owner who wants it was for** — the close named its own reopening condition and the condition was
> met. **A close that can be reopened by a named decider is the kind this document was trying to
> write; a close that could not would have been the failure mode item 49(a) records.**
>
> **One thing the planning analysis found is worth reading even by someone who never runs the
> campaign:** the four columns `tools/analyse-outcomes.py` reports **cannot answer this question at
> any n anyone will run**, and `losses` — the column carrying this project's starkest figure, 26
> against 0 — **has been degenerate since the reference-script fix.** The signal moved into the
> graded `pk` the engine has recorded on every damage line since Phase 1b and that no instrument
> here has ever computed.
>
> ***(v1.8.46 — THE CAMPAIGN RAN AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS NO LONGER THE WHOLE ANSWER. §Corrections
> item 62.)*** *"Unmeasured"* held for the life of this document and holds no longer, **on exactly
> one endpoint.** Four three-arm runs under the pre-registered rule give a paired ON − SCRIPT-ONLY
> difference in **damage absorbed** of **−0.7741, 95 % CI [−1.0210, −0.5272]**, negative in 4 of 4,
> **and it replicates against the five planning runs as an independent set.** **The commanded
> aircraft absorb roughly half the damage the same script absorbs un-commanded.**
>
> **What is still unmeasured is most of the question, and the list is not a formality.** Damage
> *dealt*, kills, launches and losses remain **unmeasured and unclaimable** at any n this project has
> run — 17 to 156 runs each, and `losses` degenerate. **So the campaign cannot separate *"the
> commander makes the aircraft safer"* from *"the commander makes it fight less"***, and that
> sentence travels with the result wherever it is quoted. One scenario, one force laydown, one
> model. **Maintenance is unaffected: no phase opened, no gate was created, the register is still
> empty, and no bar moved.**

**What maintenance does NOT mean.** It does not mean the code is frozen — defects get fixed. It does
not lower any bar: the gates that pass today are the gates that must pass tomorrow. And it does not
retire §Corrections, which **grows monotonically by design and is a history rather than a backlog** —
conflating the two is what made a two-row register feel like an unending queue.

See the subsection below.

#### The register has three states, and "open" has been doing the work of all three *(v1.8.33)*

**The defect is structural and readable off this table.** Until this revision the register recorded exactly **two** states: **closed**, by striking the id through and writing a dated result into the `Blocked on` cell; and **open**, by doing neither. So *"open"* has been carrying two incompatible meanings at once — *a live question someone should answer*, and *a dormant row nobody should touch* — and nothing in the table separated them. Of the five rows reading open at v1.8.32, **two were live (C17, C23) and three were dormant (C8, C5, C6)**. The column is headed **"Blocked on"**, and **not one of the three dormant rows was blocked on anything a person could go and do**: each cell held a *destination*, not a blocker.

**Three states, from this revision.**

| State | Marker | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| **OPEN** | plain id | Someone should do something, it is this project's to do, and it is not done |
| **DEFERRED** | `*(DEFERRED)*` on the id | Dormant on purpose. Carries a **stated position** and a **revisit condition**, and doing nothing is the correct action until that condition is met |
| **CLOSED** | `~~struck-through~~` id | A dated result, with what it does and does not establish |

**A DEFERRED row SHALL carry a revisit condition a reader can test without running anything, and SHALL state what work that condition then triggers.** A deferral naming no condition is an aspirational deferral, which is invisible debt — the same failure `tools/lint-prd.ps1`'s open-question check exists to catch, and the reason OQ-4 aged three revisions past its decision target unnoticed. **C6's condition is one directory listing; C8's is one line of AIC-API-2.** Neither needs a run, a grant or a model, which is the property that makes a dormant row auditable rather than merely quiet.

**Why this is a third state and not a second closed-row flavour.** A close asserts that nothing further is ever required. That is true of C5 and false of C8 and C6: if a non-Haiku default is proposed, real measurement is required, and if `n8ro-llm` lands, a real adapter decision is required. **Closing them would delete the only place those obligations live as live instructions**, which is how a tidy register becomes a lossy one.

**The census after this revision: OPEN — C17, C23. DEFERRED — C8, C6. CLOSED — every other row.** Two live rows, and **both are on the owner's desk rather than on an engineer's** — C17 is a decision that has been made and whose consequence is owned, C23 is a design choice between three layers. That is the fact the previous count of five was obscuring.

**The census at v1.8.41: OPEN — none. DEFERRED — none. CLOSED or CANCELLED — every row.** C17 and C23 both close in this revision; C8 closed and C6 was cancelled in v1.8.36. **This is the first time this register has been empty, and it is a state rather than an achievement:** it means every named defect has a dated result and every named decision has a decider who has decided. **One governance item is still outstanding and is deliberately NOT a row** — the standing hosted-egress authorization, which lives in §Review checklist where it has always lived, because moving it here would double-track a decision that already has a home and an owner.

#### The register records two KINDS of row, and queuing them together hid a falling severity curve *(v1.8.41)*

**Every row carries a KIND from this revision: `product` or `instrument`.** They are different urgencies for different readers and they were indistinguishable in one list.

| Kind | What it means | Who it is for | How it ends |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`product`** | A defect in what ships — the plugin, the reference script, the doctrine, the order contract. It can affect somebody running a scenario | The owner, and anyone deploying | Fixed, and the fix is demonstrable |
| **`instrument`** | A defect in what this project measures with — a harness, an analysis script, a fixture corpus, a figure quoted past its instrument | This project only. **Zero user impact by construction** | Fixed, and something now fails when it recurs |

**Why this needed saying rather than being obvious.** The last five revisions' findings, in order, are: an aircraft that stops flying (**product**), a threshold inside a settling band (**product**), a measurement harness that had not compiled in eleven revisions (**instrument**), and a fixture corpus three revisions stale (**instrument**). **That is a falling severity curve, and it was invisible while both kinds shared a list** — a reader counting open rows saw four problems rather than two-and-diminishing.

**It is a labelling change and nothing more.** No row's status moves because of it, an `instrument` row is not a lesser obligation, and **it does not license leaving one open** — item 56 is the record of what an unattended instrument costs.

#### Opening a row, from v1.8.41

**A row SHALL be opened only for one of two things:**

1. **A defect with a named mechanism** — something readable off recorded values, source, or a shipped interface. Not a suspicion, not a rate, not "this number looks wrong".
2. **A decision with a named decider** — and the decider is a person, not a phase or a date.

**Everything else goes to §Out of scope as a DEFERRED row with a revisit condition**, which is the instrument v1.8.33 built for exactly this and which already carries seven rows. **A register row for *"we should measure this someday"* is invisible debt wearing a tracker's clothes** — it is OQ-4's failure mode, and §Corrections item 49(a) is the record of what it costs.

**Why the bar goes up now.** Under §Rollout's maintenance close this register is the only tracker left, so the discipline that used to come from a phase gate has to come from the entry rule instead.

## Review checklist

- [x] All requirements have acceptance criteria
- [x] All FRs have **Customer scenario** + **Pain removed** fields
- [x] All FRs have a corresponding `UAC-{FR-ID}` entry in Appendix B
- [x] Naming/path conventions subsection present at the top of the FR section
- [x] Scope Authority subsection present
- [x] Out of Scope section present with structured entries (status / rationale / target / date)
- [x] Open Questions table has decision target + rationale on every entry; no owner column
- [x] Security implications assessed, including an enumerated transmitted-field list
- [x] Cross-component dependencies documented with in-tree verification status
- [x] Test plan covers every P1 requirement and runs without an inference server
- [x] Rollback strategy defined, with a seconds-scale first step

## Appendix A: Units and frames, traced to source

Every quantity this PRD's order schema carries, with the `schema-reference.json` record it derives from. Units live only in that file — deliberately absent from the C++ headers.

| Quantity | Unit | Frame / datum | Schema record | `unit` key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Latitude | degrees | Geodetic WGS-84 | `/datablocks/positionGeodetic/latitudeDeg` | `Deg` |
| Longitude | degrees | Geodetic WGS-84 | `/datablocks/positionGeodetic/longitudeDeg` | `Deg` |
| Altitude | metres | **Height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid (HAE)** — not AGL, not MSL | `/datablocks/positionGeodetic/altitudeHaeM` | `M` |
| Cruise / commanded speed | metres per second | Ground speed | `/datablocks/waypoint/speed` | `Mps` |
| Initial speed | metres per second | Ground speed, level flight at t=0 | `/datablocks/componentTransform/speedMps` | `Mps` |
| Heading | degrees | Clockwise from **true** north | `/datablocks/componentTransform/headingDeg` | `Deg` |
| Orbit / loiter radius | metres | — | `/datablocks/componentNavigation/onWaypointReachedLoiterRadiusM` | `M` |
| Sensor detection radius | metres | Slant range | `/datablocks/componentSensor/detectionRangeM` | `M` |
| Mission tick period | seconds | Simulation time | `/datablocks/componentMission/updateIntervalS` | `S` |

**Not in the schema** *(clarified v1.2)*. The schema export carries only what an author states, so the transform's live motion state has no record above. Two other sources own it, and which one applies depends on whether you are in Lua or C++:

| Quantity | Unit / frame | Lua source (stubs) | C++ source (runtime columns) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Velocity | m/s, NED | `entityControl.getVelocityNed` → `velN, velE, velD` | `TransformRuntimeColumns.h` — `velocityNed.x` / `.y` / `.z` (x=North, y=East, z=Down) |
| Acceleration | m/s², NED | `entityControl.getAccelerationNed` | `accelerationNed.x` / `.y` / `.z` |
| Orientation | body-to-NED | `entityControl.getOrientationEulerDeg` → `headingDeg, pitchDeg, rollDeg` | `orientationBodyToNedQuat.w` / `.x` / `.y` / `.z` (unit quaternion, **not** Euler) |

Note the two path conventions differ: the schema uses `/`, the runtime columns use `.`. The runtime columns fail *silently* on a bad path — see §Naming and path conventions and AIC-ARCH-4.

Also from the generated stubs rather than the schema: sensor tracks report `range_m` in metres and `snr_DB` in decibels — the units carried by `aiCommander.reportTrack`'s `rangeM` and `snrDb` arguments (AIC-API-1). DIS entity kind follows SISO-REF-010: 1 = platform, 2 = munition; it is *not* transmitted in v1.2 (see §Out of scope).

## Appendix B: User acceptance criteria

### UAC-AIC-ARCH-1: Three-tier decision split
**GIVEN** a scenario author running `oppint_red_interceptor` with the commander enabled
**WHEN** the entity changes posture in response to an accepted order
**THEN** every position change traces to a `navigation.*` verb invoked by the Lua script, the plugin has issued zero `entityControl.requestUpdate*` calls and zero `writeComponentField*` calls against `componentTransform`, and a commander-disabled run of the same script is byte-identical to a run with the plugin absent.

### UAC-AIC-ARCH-2: Snapshot → worker → order-slot threading
**GIVEN** an operator running the 7B model on CPU, where one order takes 10–15 s
**WHEN** a request is in flight across many simulation frames
**THEN** `onTickFrame` cost stays under 0.5 ms at p95 and 2.0 ms at p99, the worker holds no SDK pointer — a property asserted at compile time by `static_assert` over the captured types, not merely observed — the full suite is clean under AddressSanitizer (65/65), and the exchange-slot stress test completes 20,000 concurrent publishes against a concurrent consumer with no torn read detected by its second-field serial check.

*(v1.3 — this UAC previously read "TSAN reports no race". There is no ThreadSanitizer runtime for Windows, so that condition could never be met on the target platform; §Corrections item 8. The criteria above are what was actually run. They do not carry the same guarantee — AddressSanitizer finds memory errors, not races, and a stress test samples interleavings rather than proving their absence — and the gap is held open as a risk row rather than closed by restatement.)*

### UAC-AIC-ARCH-3: One `ILlmClient` seam
**GIVEN** a CI machine with no inference server and no network
**WHEN** the integration suite runs with `commander.backend = "stub"`
**THEN** the full order pipeline — render, validate, record, publish, consume from Lua — executes with no I/O, and switching `commander.backend` at runtime changes the adapter without a restart.

### UAC-AIC-ARCH-4: Runtime-column startup probe
*(Added v1.2)*
**GIVEN** a release tree in which a `componentTransform` runtime column has been renamed or is otherwise unresolvable
**WHEN** the plugin initializes and probes `velocityNed.x` / `.y` / `.z`
**THEN** the probe fails, the commander stays disabled, the failing path is named in the startup log and surfaced through `aiCommander.getStats()`, no order is requested, and at no point is a snapshot built carrying a fabricated `0, 0, 0` velocity.

### UAC-AIC-ORD-1: Order document schema
**GIVEN** a tactics author reading the order contract
**WHEN** the model returns a response carrying an unknown property, an out-of-enum posture, or an altitude outside the configured bounds
**THEN** the order is rejected with reason `schema`, `enum`, or `clamp` respectively, **no field that carries control authority is repaired**, and the previously published order remains in force.

*(v1.8.30 — this criterion read *"no field is repaired"*, which two revisions have since made untrue on purpose, and a UAC that contradicts its own FR is what stops anyone noticing the FR changed.)* **AND GIVEN** the same author reading the two exceptions: **WHEN** the model returns a `hold` order whose `reason` exceeds 512 characters, or whose `orbitRadiusM` is zero, **THEN** the order is **accepted** with the `reason` truncated and marked (v1.8.25) and the radius replaced by `safety.defaultOrbitRadiusM` and marked (v1.8.30), the posture / target / waypoint / ROE it carried are preserved intact, each substitution increments its own counter, and **an order carrying a positive `orbitRadiusM` on a posture that forbids one is still rejected `shape`** — the repairs are one-directional and are confined to fields whose value the runtime never compelled the model to supply.

### UAC-AIC-ORD-2: Posture → verb mapping
**GIVEN** the reference Tier-1 script and an accepted order with `posture = "hold"`
**WHEN** the script's `onTick` runs
**THEN** it calls `navigation.requestHoldPosition(entityId, lat, lon, alt, orbitRadiusM, cruiseSpeedMps)` with the ordered values, and no verb outside the authorized set is invoked — and in the same tick, before reading the order, it has reported its track picture via `sensor.getTrackNr` / `getTrackById` → `aiCommander.reportTrack` and its stores via `weapon.getWeaponLoadout` → `aiCommander.reportLoadout`.

### UAC-AIC-VAL-1: Two-stage validation
**GIVEN** an operator concerned about hallucinated targets
**WHEN** the model emits an order naming an entity id that Tier 1 never reported through `aiCommander.reportTrack` for the window the order's snapshot came from
**THEN** Stage B rejects it with reason `track`, one `order.rejected` record is written carrying the truncated raw body, the `aicmd.reject.track` counter increments, and no `navigation.*` or `weapon.*` verb is invoked with that id.

### UAC-AIC-VAL-2: Reject-and-retain fallback ladder
**GIVEN** an inference server that dies 200 s into a scenario
**WHEN** the run continues to completion
**THEN** the entity holds its last accepted order for `orderValidityS`, transitions to the standing order, is released to Tier 1 after `releaseAfterS`, completes the scenario under Tier-1 behaviour, and each transition is recorded exactly once — **and on every one of those three rungs it still defends itself against an inbound munition, still selects and engages targets under its own launch discipline, and still egresses winchester.** *(v1.8.30 — the last clause is the requirement, not a gloss on it. This criterion previously ended at `resumeWaypointFollowing`, and an entity that resumes waypoint following while being shot at satisfies every word of it: **22 of 24 commanded aircraft were destroyed across twelve pairs against 0 of 24 controls, and no acceptance criterion in this document could see it.** The measurable form is AIC-VAL-2's new criterion — launches, detonations and survival within a stated tolerance of the same scenario on the shipped script.)*

### UAC-AIC-SEC-2: Transmitted-field allowlist
**GIVEN** an owner who must state what proprietary data leaves the machine
**WHEN** a prompt is rendered from a snapshot whose every string field carries a unique sentinel
**THEN** only allowlisted sentinels appear in the rendered bytes, no `componentTrackIdentity` sentinel appears, **no `domain` attribute and no scenario team *name* appears on any track row**, and the API key value appears in no prompt, log, or order record. *(v1.8.30 — this read *"no `team` / `kind` / `domain` attribute"*; `kind` and `team` are now transmitted as closed vocabularies.)* **AND** a track reported with an out-of-vocabulary `kind` or `team` renders as `other` / `unknown` rather than passing the value through, so **no string outside the five-value and three-value sets can reach the prompt by this path** — which is the property that keeps the widened row from being the free-text channel §Out of scope's cost clause was about.

### UAC-AIC-API-1: The `aiCommander` Lua namespace
**GIVEN** a Tier-1 script author who has run the engine once to regenerate stubs
**WHEN** they call `aiCommander.getPosture(entityId)` for an entity with no order, with a valid order, and with a malformed argument
**THEN** they receive `nil, nil, nil`; the ordered posture/target/speed triple; and `nil, nil, nil` respectively — never a raised error — and `aiCommander.lua` in the stubs folder documents all fourteen signatures.

### UAC-AIC-API-1b: Tier-1 track and loadout ingress
*(Added v1.2)*
**GIVEN** a commanded entity whose script reports three tracks and two hardpoints in one cadence window
**WHEN** the next snapshot is taken and an order naming the second reported track comes back
**THEN** the prompt carried exactly those three tracks in ascending `targetEntityId` order with only `targetEntityId` / `rangeM` / `snrDb` / `kind` / `team` per row *(v1.8.30 — arity 4 → 6)*, Stage-B B3 accepts the order, the reported lists were cleared when the snapshot was taken — and an order naming a fourth, unreported id would have been rejected `track` instead. **AND** a fourth track reported with an unrecognised `kind` is still carried, as `other`, rather than the call returning false and the track vanishing from the picture.

### UAC-AIC-ORD-2b: The reference script keeps fighting when the commander is silent
*(Added v1.8.30)*
**GIVEN** the commander-aware reference script deployed with `commander.enabled = false` — no plugin orders, no inference server, no model
**WHEN** the scenario runs to completion
**THEN** the entity manoeuvres against an inbound munition inside the script's threat range on the tick it is detected, selects and engages hostile air targets under its own launch discipline from a hardpoint whose envelope covers the range, egresses when winchester, and its launch count, detonation count and survival are within the harness's stated tolerance of the same scenario flown on the shipped `oppint_red_interceptor.lua` — **and it reports no contact whose team equals its own.**

### UAC-AIC-API-2: Plugin configuration surface
**GIVEN** a platform owner configuring the plugin
**WHEN** they set `commander.backend = "claude"` while `claude.enabled` is false, or set `claude.baseUrl` to an `http://` URL
**THEN** `applyConfigFields` returns false, every prior value is unchanged, a reason is logged, and no hosted request is ever issued.

### UAC-AIC-BE-1: Local adapter
**GIVEN** a local inference server on `local.baseUrl`
**WHEN** the commander requests an order and the server is unreachable
**THEN** the transport failure (`send()` returning `std::nullopt`) is distinguished from a returned response carrying a non-2xx status in the reject reason, the worker's `IHttpClient` instance is used by no other thread, and the configured timeout is honoured.

### UAC-AIC-BE-2: Claude adapter
**GIVEN** an authorized Phase 2 run against `claude-haiku-4-5`
**WHEN** the API returns `stop_reason == "refusal"`
**THEN** the refusal is detected before `content` is read, the order is rejected with reason `refusal`, no `effort` parameter was sent, and the response's token counts are written to the order record — *(v1.8.18)* including **both** `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`, carried on the adapter's result value rather than readable only through a concrete adapter pointer, and present on the **rejected** record as well as the accepted one.

### UAC-AIC-BE-3: Prompt prefix stability
**GIVEN** a run with a fixed configuration
**WHEN** 100 prompts are rendered from 100 different snapshots
**THEN** the prefix bytes are identical across all 100, the prefix contains no timestamp/entity id/counter, startup logs `prefixBytes`, and **the build pins that byte count to the artifact that was measured** — `tests/PromptRendererTests.cpp` asserts the shipped prefix is exactly **8,750 bytes** when built from the repository's `data/doctrine.txt`, and asserts the **1,818 bytes** `PromptRenderer::build` contributes around the doctrine, so a doctrine edit and a renderer edit each fail with their own message.

*(v1.8.16 — **this criterion previously asserted a startup comparison of the derived token count against the configured model's cache minimum, and that comparison has never existed in the code.** It was written in v1.3, reasoned about in v1.8.2 and v1.8.4 as though it were running, and cited in §Cost model as "the guard". The startup line logs `prefixBytes=` and stops. §Corrections item 33(a) records it. **What is asserted above is what is implemented**, and the difference matters beyond bookkeeping: a UAC that claims a guard exists is the thing that stops anyone writing one.)*

***(v1.8.18 — the runtime half is specified and this criterion now covers both halves. What follows describes behaviour that AIC-BE-3 requires; the paragraphs below it are kept as the record of why the shape is what it is.)***

**GIVEN** a run on the hosted backend against a model whose cache minimum this document lists
**WHEN** each response arrives with its `usage` block
**THEN** the plugin compares `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` against that model's minimum, stays silent on a **cold start** (`creation > 0`, `read == 0`) and on a healthy hit (`read ≥ minimum`), warns **once per run** when **both** are zero — the block never cached — with the model, the minimum, both observed values and the per-order cost consequence in the line, treats an unrecognised `claude.model` as **unknown** rather than guessing a bound, and writes both fields into every `order.accepted` **and** `order.rejected` record. The check reads the response's `usage`, never `prefix()`.

**The runtime half was deliberately absent and carried as C9 through v1.8.17, and the two paragraphs below record why it could not simply be written.** It cannot be written against `prefix()` — AIC-BE-3 v1.8.4(a) establishes that reading the prefix alone is wrong by 69 % about the quantity it guards, and after C3 the prefix text is ~2,212 tokens against a 4,096 minimum, so a `prefix()`-based check would emit a false shortfall warning on **every** run. It has to compare `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`, which is **5,118 tokens per hit** and clears the minimum by 1,022 (24.9 %). That value did not reach the sim thread: `LlmResult` carried no cache field, so AIC-BE-2's own recording `SHALL` was unmet as well (§Corrections item 33(f)). **One missing field, both halves, one carried item.**

**And it is not a *startup* comparison in any case.** The first request of a run is always a cache **write** and reads zero — 119 of 120 in C3's arms, 95 of 96 in C2's. A check that fires at startup has nothing to read; the earliest honest moment is the second response of a run. ***(v1.8.18 — and that "second response" framing is now sharpened by the second field: the cold first response is identifiable rather than merely skippable, because it writes the block and says so. The check does not have to ignore the first response; it can read it correctly.)***

### UAC-AIC-BE-4: TLS availability
**GIVEN** a target machine whose OpenSSL runtime is missing
**WHEN** the first hosted request is issued
**THEN** the `https` request returns `std::nullopt` while a plain-`http` control request to the same host returns a value, the plugin logs a TLS-availability diagnosis distinct from a generic transport failure, disables the hosted backend, and falls back per the ladder without retrying in a tight loop.

### UAC-AIC-DET-1: Order record format
**GIVEN** an engineer investigating a break-off at t=412 s
**WHEN** they read the order log
**THEN** they find the `order.requested` and `order.accepted` records for that entity and serial, with snapshot and prompt hashes, latency, token counts, and the full order including the model's stated reason — and no API key and no `componentTrackIdentity` field anywhere in the file. *(v1.8.18 — the token counts are four fields, not two: `tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheCreationTokens`, and they appear on `order.rejected` as well, so an engineer pricing a run does not have to assume the rejected orders were free. Item 27(d) measured four that were not.)*

### UAC-AIC-DET-2: Replay mode
**GIVEN** a recorded order log and a machine with no inference server
**WHEN** the run is replayed twice with `commander.backend = "replay"`
**THEN** both replays publish byte-identical order sequences at identical simulation times, no `IHttpClient` is constructed, Stage B still runs, and any divergence from live state produces a `replay.divergence` record rather than silent acceptance.

## Appendix C: Architecture decision records

> Stubs capturing this PRD's major decisions. Expand into full ADRs in the project decision log as implementation proceeds.

### ADR-1: Confine the language model to a Tier-2 intent layer

**Status:** Proposed
**Context:** `extension-points.md:140` states that scripting is a decision layer and authoritative state mutation stays in C++. Measured inference latency is 3–6 s (3B, CPU) to 10–15 s (7B, CPU), against a simulation running at frame cadence.
**Decision:** The model emits structured intent — posture, target, waypoint, ROE — every N seconds. Tier 1 validates and executes it with existing verbs. Tier 0 flies the entity. The model is never in the control loop and cannot express raw kinematics, structurally: the order schema has no property for heading, velocity, or acceleration.
**Consequences:**
- Inference latency becomes irrelevant to simulation correctness.
- The existing quality of `oppint_red_interceptor.lua` is preserved rather than replaced.
- The commander cannot react to fast events; Tier 1 must act correctly on a stale order, which is an explicit design obligation.

### ADR-2: One `ILlmClient` seam with four adapters, selected by config

**Status:** Proposed
**Context:** Phase 1 is local inference; Phase 2 adds a hosted API. No inference server ships in the tree, so CI needs a path with no server at all. `n8ro-llm` may land later.
**Decision:** A single interface taking a rendered prompt and returning a raw body or a transport failure, with `stub`, `replay`, `local`, and `claude` adapters chosen by `commander.backend`. Validation, recording, and publication are adapter-independent.
**Consequences:**
- CI runs the full pipeline deterministically with no server and no network.
- Phase 2 is a config change, not a fork.
- A future `n8ro-llm` message-bus path is a fifth adapter, not a redesign.
- Cost: an indirection and a lifecycle to manage for four implementations, three of which do no real work.

### ADR-3: Snapshot-by-value across a latest-wins slot

**Status:** Proposed
**Context:** `IPlugin.h:36` guarantees callbacks on a single update thread; `IHttpClient::send()` is blocking and single-thread-only; `ScriptingApiContext`'s collaborators are single-thread-only. `IThreadRunner::submitBackgroundTask` exists but `PluginContext::threadRunner` is nullable.
**Decision:** The sim thread builds a POD snapshot and publishes it to a mutex-guarded latest-wins slot. A worker copies it, runs inference and syntactic validation, and publishes a candidate order to a second slot. The sim thread drains that slot, runs semantic validation against live state, and publishes. The worker holds no SDK pointer.
**Consequences:**
- The sim thread never blocks on inference.
- Semantic checks that need `IEntityManager` stay where they are legal, which is why validation is two-stage rather than one.
- Stale snapshots are dropped rather than queued — correct, because a stale snapshot produces a stale order.
- Cost: the validator is split across two locations and must be read as one pipeline.
- *(v1.2)* The snapshot carries the Tier-1-reported track and loadout lists captured at snapshot time, and Stage-B B3 validates against *that* captured list rather than whatever is current at publication — otherwise a target legitimately visible when the order was requested could be rejected merely because inference outlived the cadence window.

### ADR-4: Record every order from day one; replay is a first-class backend

**Status:** Proposed
**Context:** `execution-models-and-timing.md` treats reproducibility as a design goal. An LLM in the loop breaks it outright, and retrofitting a record format after the fact never captures what the investigation actually needs.
**Decision:** JSONL order log on by default, carrying snapshot and prompt hashes, latency, token counts, and the full order. `replay` is an `ILlmClient` adapter, not a special mode — it goes through the same validation and publication path.
**Consequences:**
- A run is investigable and reproducible at the decision layer.
- CI gets a deterministic full-pipeline test.
- The guarantee is honest and bounded: identical *orders* at identical simulation times; trajectory reproducibility is inherited from the engine's timing configuration, not provided here.
- Cost: ~700 KB of log per scenario-hour, and a rotation policy to maintain.

### ADR-5: Credentials by environment-variable name, never by value

**Status:** Proposed
**Context:** `PluginConfigField` values are canonical strings persisted by the host. Every file in this tree carries a proprietary/confidential header.
**Decision:** `claude.apiKeyEnvVar` stores the *name* of an environment variable. The value is read via `std::getenv` at request time, never persisted, never logged, never returned by `getConfigFields()`. `claude.enabled` is a second, independent switch defaulting false, and an egress always logs a warning naming its destination.
**Consequences:**
- No credential is written to disk by the plugin.
- Data egress requires two positive acts and is always visible in the log.
- Cost: operators must set an environment variable before a run, which is friction — deliberate friction, on the one action in this design that cannot be undone.

### ADR-6: Tier 1 reports the tactical picture; the plugin does not fetch it

**Status:** Proposed *(added v1.2)*
**Context:** Sensor tracks and weapon loadout are runtime state with no public C++ read seam — no track component in the schema or `ComponentTypeNames.h`, no `IEntityManager` accessor, and no `ComponentFieldAccess` reader for the `list`-typed loadout. Both are reachable only from Lua, via `sensor.getTrackNr` / `getTrackById` and `weapon.getWeaponLoadout`. Three options were considered: add Lua ingress verbs; drop tracks and loadout from the snapshot; or synthesize a track list by scanning the entity roster.
**Decision:** Tier 1 pushes what it already sees, through `aiCommander.reportTrack` and `aiCommander.reportLoadout` (AIC-API-1). The plugin never reconstructs a tactical picture by other means, and roster-scanning is explicitly out of scope.
**Consequences:**
- The commander's view of the world is exactly the deterministic script's view. It cannot see further than the entity's own sensors, which is both correct and the honest reading of "the model issues intent, the script owns the facts".
- AIC-SEC-2 tightens: nothing reaches a prompt that a script did not hand over, the ingress verbs carry scalars only, and `team` / `kind` / `domain` leave the transmitted set.
- Stage-B B3 becomes a check against reported state rather than an engine query, so it validates the model against what the script actually observed — which is the comparison that matters for catching a hallucinated target.
- Reporting is advisory: a script that reports nothing still gets orders, but cannot receive a targeted one. The degradation is legible rather than silent.
- Cost: the Lua surface grows from 12 functions to 14, and the reference script carries an obligation it would not otherwise have. Accepted, because the alternative that needed no new verbs — roster synthesis — would have fed the validator a fiction and made B3 worse than useless.

### ADR-7: Substitute structural and stress evidence for a race detector

**Status:** Proposed *(added v1.3)*
**Context:** AIC-ARCH-2's threading claim was to be substantiated by a clean ThreadSanitizer run. No TSan runtime exists for this platform: VS 2026 Insiders ships `tsan_interface.h` / `tsan_interface_atomic.h` with no `clang_rt.tsan` library, and neither MSVC nor the bundled LLVM toolchain supports TSan on Windows, while ASan, UBSan, and the fuzzer runtimes all ship complete. The gate as written could not be passed by any build on the target platform.
**Decision:** Carry the threading claim on three artifacts instead — a `static_assert`-enforced value-only worker capture with a deep-copy-outlives-original test (structural), a 20,000-publish exchange-slot stress test with a serial encoded into a second field so torn reads are detected (empirical, targeted at the single crossing point), and the full suite clean under AddressSanitizer at 65/65 (excludes the memory-error class). State the residual gap versus a real race detector in §Risks and record race detection in §Out of scope rather than declaring the concern closed.
**Consequences:**
- The gate becomes passable and, more importantly, *meaningful*: an unsatisfiable checklist item trains reviewers to wave the checklist through, which costs more than the coverage it pretends to provide.
- The load-bearing argument moves from detection to structure. A worker that provably captures nothing shared is a stronger statement about *sharing* than any detector run, and it is checked at compile time on every build rather than in one CI job.
- What is lost is real and is not recovered by any of the three: no happens-before analysis, no coverage of unexecuted interleavings, and no visibility into reorderings x86-64's memory model hides. The design is not proven race-free; it is argued race-free and stress-corroborated.
- Cost: the residual risk is permanent for as long as the plugin is Windows-only. If it is ever built for a platform with a TSan runtime, running it there is the cheapest available closure and should be taken.

## Quality gate notes

Advisory. Gaps found while composing this PRD, not blockers.

- **Two dependencies are unresolvable from inside this tree.** The inference server (OQ-1, OQ-2) and the entitlement gate (OQ-5) both need answers from outside the release tree. Phases 0 and 1a are fully deliverable and testable without either, which is why the `stub` backend is Phase 1a's gate rather than a convenience.
- **Success metrics carry no historical baselines** because no implementation exists. Every baseline reads "N/A"; targets are derived from the brief's measured latency budget and from the engine's own frame cadence. The first Phase 1b run establishes real baselines and this section should be revised against them.
- **H1 is the load-bearing hypothesis and is the hardest to measure objectively.** "Posture transitions a reviewer marks appropriate" is a human judgment. If Phase 1b needs a harder signal, candidates are: time-to-first-valid-shot, shots per kill, and survival rate across paired runs — all computable from the existing entity logs. Worth deciding before the Phase 1b gate rather than during it.
- **OQ-4 was answered, one revision late, and the delay cost nothing.** *(v1.4.)* It was scheduled at the Phase 1a gate so it would land before Phase 1b spent effort on the local adapter. Phase 1a closed without it — caught by the v1.3 PRD review, then resolved. The answer was "no", so nothing built in Phase 1a was wasted; had it been "yes", the slip would have been expensive, and that asymmetry is the argument for answering cheap-but-invalidating questions on schedule rather than when convenient. The investigation took under an hour: enumerate the tool handlers in the shipped binary.
- **The doctrine text is unwritten and is on the critical path for order quality.** It is the one Phase 1 deliverable this PRD does not specify in detail, because its content is domain expertise rather than engineering. Flagged as a rabbit hole with a one-day timebox; if it needs more, that is a signal to reconsider the RAG deferral.
- **v1.3 note — a validation gate must name a tool that exists on the target platform.** "TSAN clean" survived from the authoring brief through two revisions and a design pass without anyone checking whether a ThreadSanitizer runtime ships for Windows. It does not, and the PRD consequently specified a gate no build could ever pass. The lesson generalizes past this one item: a gate is a claim about *this* toolchain, and every gate item should be traceable to a command someone has run here, in the same way §Corrections requires every SDK fact to be traceable to a shipped header. The other gate items were checked against this when v1.3 was written — `dumpbin /exports`, `/fsanitize=address`, and the replay suite all exist and all run — but the check should be part of writing a gate, not part of repairing one.
- **v1.3 note — two Phase 1a gate items were assumptions wearing the costume of measurements.** "TSAN clean" was unrunnable and the Cost model's ~800-token prefix was a guess that undershot the measured 1,200 by a third, carrying every uncached figure in the table down with it. Both were phrased with the confidence of observed facts. The pattern to watch: a number with no units-and-source trace behind it (Appendix A's discipline) reads exactly like one that has been measured, and the Cost model — the one section whose whole output is arithmetic — had no such trace on its most load-bearing input. §Corrections item 9 now carries it.
- **v1.2 note — the snapshot was specified from the Lua surface, not the C++ one.** Every field in the original §Exactly what is transmitted named a Lua verb, and two of them turned out to have no C++ equivalent. The lesson generalizes: for a C++ plugin, "which verb returns this?" is the wrong traceability question — "which header or schema record exposes this to *the plugin*?" is the right one. Appendix A now carries the Lua/C++ split explicitly so the next field added is checked against both columns.

## Changelog

### v1.8.47 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 63: the owner authorized hosted egress, and the first thing that authorization needs is the control it was drafted against — a spend ceiling, specified before any code.** No run, no network, no cost, no code, **and no request is made under the authorization by this revision.**

**The owner authorized egress on 2026-08-09**, answering the box v1.8.44 drafted. **The box is not ticked here.** That draft named three conditions a standing grant must carry, and **condition ① does not exist** — there is no spend ceiling anywhere in the shipped code. **A grant recorded against a control that does not exist is the paperwork this project spent forty revisions learning not to write.** The ceiling is built first; the grant is recorded next, naming it.

**Opened as C24 — the register's first row since it emptied at v1.8.41** — under the entry rule, as a defect readable off a shipped interface. Under six *measurement* grants the missing ceiling was safe because **every run was individually authorized, costed and recorded, so a human checkpoint sat in front of every request this project ever made.** The defect is old; the control that masked it is what is going away.

**Specified in AIC-BE-2:** the adapter accumulates cost for the life of the process and **latches off** at `claude.maxSpendUsd`, logging once — **a ceiling that is re-checked but not latched spends one more request every cadence forever.** It **fails closed**: at or below zero disables the hosted backend rather than meaning unlimited, because **the failure mode of an unset or mis-parsed field must be "sends nothing"**. Default **1.00 USD**. **The four unit prices are configuration, not constants**, since `claude.model` is operator-settable — the shape of item 54(e)'s doctrine defect. The refusal reaches the **existing** reject-and-retain ladder as a transport failure naming the budget: no new reject reason, and no silent stop.

**What it does not bound: it is per-process.** It bounds any single engine session — the exposure item 60(d) derived — and not running the engine a hundred times. **Deliberate: starting a run is a human act, and that checkpoint covers repetition.**

Running total unchanged at **≈$2.57 of $5**.

### v1.8.46 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 62: the outcome campaign ran, the pre-registered rule returns CLAIM SUPPORTED, and what the commander is worth is measured for the first time — on one endpoint, in one scenario, at one model.** Four three-arm 600 s `local` runs at the shipped default, **22 checks / 0 failed** each. No network beyond the local backend, no hosted egress, no grant, no cost.

**The result, against the rule committed before the first run.** Paired ON − SCRIPT-ONLY on `damageAbsorbed`: **mean −0.7741, sd 0.1552, 95 % CI [−1.0210, −0.5272], t = −9.976 on 3 df, p = 0.0021**, negative in **4 of 4** runs. All three conjuncts met. **The commanded aircraft absorb roughly half the damage the same script absorbs un-commanded.**

**It replicates against an independent set and the two are deliberately not pooled.** Planning runs **−0.6835 [−0.9351, −0.4319]**; campaign **−0.7741 [−1.0210, −0.5272]**. Same sign, overlapping intervals, disjoint data. **This project has four results that did not survive their own repeat — items 40, 42, 47(b), 50(a) — and this is the first one that has.**

**A claim v1.8.42 made is refuted by the campaign it was written for.** Item 58(g)'s *"Blue fires exactly two munitions at the commanded pair, 15 of 15 — the denominator is not a sampling quantity"* is wrong: **in one run Blue fired three.** The denominator is 9 in the ON arm against 8 in each control. **Fifteen for fifteen was a property of the sample that this document promoted to a property of the scenario.** It strengthens the result rather than threatening it — **the ON arm was shot at more and absorbed less.**

**The mechanism holds and widens:** **5 of 9** Blue munitions defeated in the commanded arm, every one with a logged `[seeker] … lost`; **0 of 8** and **0 of 8** in the controls. Pooled with the archive, **9 of 19 against 0 of 36.** Reported beside the endpoint, never merged into it.

**THE CONFOUND STANDS.** This design cannot separate *"safer"* from *"fights less"* — `damageDealt` needs ~156 runs — and its observed difference is **not** used as an argument in either direction. **No secondary endpoint is claimed**; several point the way an author would like and are archived, not concluded.

**In-engine acceptance regenerated:** **71.1 % [66.4, 75.5] → 80.8 % [77.4, 83.8]** over 609 resolved orders across 30 runs, **90.9 % [88.2, 93.2]** excluding the two non-model classes. **The C23 stall-floor class did not grow by a single sample — still 58.**

### v1.8.45 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 61: clause 8 fired in a commanded scenario for the first time, and it caught the aircraft on the way down rather than at the bottom.** One 400 s `local` run at the shipped default, archived `20260809T182353Z-c8-probe`, **8 checks / 0 failed.** No network beyond the local backend, no hosted egress, no grant, no cost.

**The residual v1.8.41 recorded is discharged.** C23's close said clause 8 had never fired in a commanded scenario and that a net which has never caught anything is not thereby proven. It has now caught something, **commander asserted ON from the startup log, 40 orders requested and 39 accepted during the run.**

**The sequence:** injection at t=90.1 at 320.0000 m/s; **−20 m/s²** through 46 injected hold calls; at t=103.9 **the shipped script** logs *"below flying speed at 47.0000 m/s; Tier 1 takes navigation"*; above the floor again at t=104.5 at 53.0000 m/s — **0.6 s against a 20 s cadence window**; the latch clears at *"recovered to 101.0 m/s"*; back to 320.0000 at **+20 m/s²**, the exact mirror and the same figure the v1.8.38 probe measured from the other end.

**The number that matters is 47, not 0.6.** The archived failure mode coasts to **1.5000 m/s and latches there for ~400 s**. Clause 8 intercepted this one **one sample below the floor**, so the latch state was never reached.

**C23 stays closed:** its reopen condition is more than one cadence window below the floor, and this was 0.6 s of 20 — by the operation of the design under test.

**A corroboration the run was not looking for:** the order accepted at t=104.4, mid-recovery, carries `cruiseSpeedMps = 121` — **the speed echo happening live during a clause 8 recovery.** Clause 8 ignored it, because it re-accelerates to Tier 1's own value and never to a speed read from an order. At 121 m/s the aircraft was already above the floor, so this echo could not have re-stalled it; **the echo under recovery is demonstrated, a re-stall averted is not.**

**The within-run control held:** `RedSu35_01`, never injected, went below the floor in 0 samples.

**THE STALL WAS INJECTED.** No ordinary order path to clause 8 is known — clause 7 prevents every naturally occurring onset — and that qualification travels with the result.

Running total unchanged at **≈$2.57 of $5**.

### v1.8.44 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 60: the last unticked box of this project's own gets a draft in front of the owner — and drafting it found that a standing grant currently has nothing to stand on.** **No run, no network, no cost, and NO GRANT.** The draft authorizes nothing, the §Review checklist box **stays unticked**, and no hosted request may be made under it.

**The finding: there is no spend ceiling anywhere in the shipped code.** `CommanderConfig.h` has `claude.enabled`, `claude.model`, `claude.maxTokens` and `claude.apiKeyEnvVar` — no per-run, per-day or cumulative bound and no counter that could enforce one. **The `$5` budget is a convention maintained by hand and enforced by nothing.** Under six measurement grants that was safe because **every run was individually authorized, costed and recorded, so a human checkpoint sat in front of every request.** A standing authorization removes exactly that checkpoint.

**The exposure, derived:** ≈$0.001223 per order, 6 orders/min on two entities, **≈$0.44/hour**; a ten-minute smoke ≈$0.073. ### v1.8.43 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 59: clause 8's third instrument is specified — the one that exercises it in a commanded scenario, which nothing has ever done.** No run, no network, no cost, no grant, and no code: specified first, per §Scope authority.

**The gap is the one v1.8.41 recorded rather than carried.** Across the two post-fix three-arm runs `navigation.requestHoldPosition` was called zero times and **clause 8 never fired once**, because clause 7 took all 33 `hold` orders and prevented the onset. That is the designed relationship between the clauses — and it leaves the safety net's whole evidence as the offline suite, which has no aircraft, plus one probe run with the commander asserted OFF.

**More scenario repeats cannot close it, and the argument is item 51(f)'s one clause downstream.** Clause 8 sits below clause 7; nothing else in this scenario stalls an aircraft; so **clause 7 working correctly is exactly what keeps clause 8 unexercised, and every further run makes that more true rather than less.** The below-floor state has to be injected, the way `tools/c23-hold-probe.lua` injected the distant hold the model would never order.

**The instrument is the shipped script plus an injector, and that distinction is the design.** `tools/c8-floor-probe.lua` is `lua/ai_commander_interceptor.lua` **unmodified** — clauses 7 and 8 are the shipped code, not a re-implementation — plus a time-boxed injector calling `navigation.requestHoldPosition` at the aircraft's own position, the one call clause 7 forbids. **The injector stops the instant the aircraft is below the floor, and everything after that is the shipped clause 8 acting alone**, with the commander ON and orders flowing.

**What it will prove, and what it will not, written before it runs.** It proves clause 8 fires, takes navigation, and recovers the aircraft within one cadence window **while a live commander publishes orders**. It does **not** prove any ordinary order path reaches clause 8 — none is known in this scenario, the probe does not invent one, and **the stall is injected, which every quotation of the result must say.**

**The criterion is extended rather than rewritten**, on v1.8.41's own precedent: three instruments, each asserting what it can see, all three named. `lua/ai_commander_interceptor.lua` is untouched, no bar moves, and no register row opens.

As paired ON − SCRIPT-ONLY differences over the five archived three-arm runs, **all four need an infeasible n** — 17, 42, 140 runs — and **`losses` is degenerate, identically 0 in all three arms of all five runs since the reference-script fix.** The column that carried this project's starkest figure, 26 against 0, now carries no information at all.

### v1.8.38 — 2026-08-09

**§Corrections item 54: C23's confirming run answers both open questions, demonstrates a claim this document had only argued, and finds a defect in the fix that nothing offline could have found.** Two ~2-minute local runs with the commander **asserted off** and no model in the loop. No network, no cost, no grant.

**Q1 — a `hold` ordered far away stops the aircraft too, and the trigger is the orbit boundary.** Ordered 20 km out at radius 5,000 and 320 m/s, both aircraft held **320.0000 m/s for fifty seconds while outside**, then decelerated **in the first sample after crossing inside** — 5,260 m outside at t=61.2, 4,972 m inside at t=62.1, **302.0000 at t=63.0** — at **−20 m/s²** to the 1.5000 latch. The archive's 16.5–17.1 s onset delay was its 20 s sampling; the real delay is under a second. **So clause 7's per-tick test is the only reading that covers this case:** an order-issue-time test would have handed exactly this order to the engine.

**Q2 — the recovery is achieved, not merely commanded.** From exactly **1.5000 m/s**, a commanded 300 m/s put both aircraft above `safety.minSpeedMps` in **3.1 seconds** against clause 8's one-cadence-window criterion, at **+20 m/s²**. This discharges the caveat that was keeping C23 open.

**And rung 2's geometry stalls an aircraft by itself.** Holding at the aircraft's own position — AIC-VAL-2 rung 2's published waypoint — with no model and no commander: **220.0000 → 1.5000 in 23 seconds**, latched. Item 53(g) was an inference from the specification; this is the behaviour.

**The run found a defect in the fix.** A recovering aircraft settles at **132.2–146.5 m/s** under a continuing 300 m/s command, and the archive says the same from the other side. **`kResumeFlyingSpeedMps` was 150.0 — inside that band — so the recovery latch might never have cleared.** Now **100.0**, with a test pinning the ceiling at 132.2. Neither the offline suite nor the archive could have found this.

**§Corrections item 49: three of the five rows this document called "open" were dormant, and the register had no way to say so.** No run, no network, no cost, no grant, no engine, no inference server. **No verdict moves and no measured figure changes.**

**The register recorded two states and needed three.** §Carried out of Phase 3 marks a row **closed** by striking its id through and writing a dated result into the `Blocked on` cell, and **open** by doing neither. So *"open"* has carried two incompatible meanings at once — *a live question someone should answer* and *a dormant row nobody should touch* — and the table **read five open rows when the honest answer was two.** The column is headed *"Blocked on"* and **not one of C8, C5 or C6 was blocked on anything a person could go and do**; each cell held a destination. This is a **MECHANISM**, readable off the document, and it survived precisely because every individual row was accurate.

| State | Marker | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| **OPEN** | plain id | Someone should do something, it is this project's to do, and it is not done |
| **DEFERRED** | `*(DEFERRED)*` on the id | Dormant on purpose, with a stated position and a revisit condition |
| **CLOSED** | `~~struck-through~~` id | A dated result, with what it does and does not establish |

**A DEFERRED row SHALL carry a revisit condition a reader can test without running anything, and SHALL state what work that condition then triggers.** C6's is one directory listing; C8's is one line of AIC-API-2.

**C5 CLOSES — a bounded negative, on the mechanism and explicitly not on the rate.** The Perth substitution (**−31.952876, 115.860450** against an own-ship near Guam, reproduced on a second entity to four decimal places, on a value appearing nowhere in the prompt) is answerable off a recorded value, so rule 4 permits one run to answer it — and the answer is the standing argument for Stage B's geofence, since **the bound is what caught it.** **No rate:** n = 11, and the detector greps for Perth specifically. **It closes because its destination closed without it** — Phase 3 ended at v1.8.17 and order quality was never measured at scale in it. **The close carries item 48(e) forward as a rule: a bounded negative at n = 11 SHALL NOT lead any summary of this project.**

**C6 is DEFERRED and reclassified: a DEPENDENCY row, not a work row.** It cannot close — OQ-3's answer is not this project's to give — and **nothing in this project is blocked on it.** Its decision target read *"v1.1 planning"* for thirty-three revisions, and a date is not a condition; it is now **`n8ro-llm` appearing in the release tree** (a DLL in `bin/`, an import library in `lib/`, or headers under `include/`), **re-verified absent 2026-08-08**. §Out of scope's row pointed at OQ-3 while OQ-3 pointed at a date, so the two deferred to each other and neither named an observable; **both now name the same one.** The Review checklist's **three** unticked boxes are reconciled as **two governance decisions plus one external dependency**, per `open-issues-review.md` Appendix A.

| `additionalProperties: false` *(control)* | an extra field | `{"p": "x"}` | YES |

The numeric half has never worked.** And the hosted path cannot express it either: `pinToConst` converts only a **zero-width** range, so the hold branch's `[1, 50000]` survives it untouched and is then stripped whole by the unsupported-keyword removal. There is no `const` equivalent for *"greater than zero."* **The rule is enforced by nothing, on either backend, except Stage A rejecting the whole order.** An explicit prompt rule was tested and fails on 4 of 5 models including the default, so the cheapest remedy is off the table. AIC-ORD-1 now **repairs** the field with `safety.defaultOrbitRadiusM`.

**§Corrections item 41: C15 was never the model's defect. C16 is decided. ### v1.8.18 — 2026-08-05

**§Corrections item 35 — the cache-accounting seam, specified before the code.** No new request, no network, no cost. No measurement, gate result, or §Success metrics row moves.

**What changed and why it is one revision rather than three.** C9 (the cache-minimum guard's runtime half), AIC-BE-2's unmet `cache_read_input_tokens` `SHALL`, and C4 (`cache_creation_input_tokens`, parsed by nothing) were three rows opened fourteen revisions apart. They are one seam, and the reason they close together is not bundling convenience — **C4's field is what makes C9's guard correct.**

- **AIC-BE-2** — the SHALL is widened: **both** cache fields SHALL be parsed and SHALL cross the worker boundary on the adapter's result value, not be reachable only through a concrete adapter pointer.
- **AIC-BE-3** — the runtime guard is specified for the first time since it was asserted in v1.3: what it compares (`usage`, **never** `prefix()`), when it may fire (per response, silent on the cold write), what it emits (one latched warning carrying the arithmetic), and which minimum it compares against. **The model → cache-minimum table is added and derived**: Haiku 4.5 **4,096**, Sonnet 5 **1,024**, Opus 5 **512** — with the property that makes it load-bearing, that **the series is not monotonic**, so an unlisted model's minimum SHALL NOT be interpolated.
- **AIC-DET-1** — both fields land on `order.accepted` **and** `order.rejected`. The rejection half is wider than C4 and C9 asked for and closes a hole item 27(d) already measured: four truncated Sonnet orders billed for 512 output tokens each that produced nothing, against a rejected record that carries no token field at all.
- **UAC-AIC-BE-2, UAC-AIC-BE-3, UAC-AIC-DET-1** — amended. UAC-AIC-BE-3 now describes **both** halves; the paragraphs explaining why the runtime half could not simply be written are kept rather than deleted.
- **§Cost model** — the paragraph that spends the 1,022-token margin records that the guard now has two halves covering **two different failures**: the build-time pin catches a prefix edit made *here*, the runtime check catches a doctrine file edited *in the release tree*, a model swapped for one with a higher minimum, or a block failing to cache for a reason unrelated to its size.
- **§Source control** — the run-evidence convention is written down (§Corrections item 35(f)). Order logs and engine logs are archived **outside** the repository; the synthetic per-order CSVs under `tests/live/data/` stay in-tree, and the line between them is *provenance*, not field set — the same boundary four egress grants held.

**The technical core, stated once.** A block under the model's cache minimum caches **silently** and reports `cache_creation_input_tokens: 0`. A cold-but-eligible first request reports it **non-zero** with zero reads. So `(0, 0)` is a shortfall and `(>0, 0)` is a healthy cold start — **and with only the read field the two are the same observation.** A guard built on `cache_read_input_tokens` alone therefore either fires on the first request of every run and gets muted, or suppresses the first response and cannot see a shortfall that begins there. C4's row said to add the field "when a cheaper reason to touch that interface arises"; **that row was wrong about its own priority, and saying so is part of this item.**

**C9 and C4 CLOSE.** Running total unchanged at **≈$2.50 of $5**.
